relevance_note: The paper reports ALDH5A1 genotypes for patients 'in whom SSADH deficiency was diagnosed' (54 families) and gives an individual-level feature for one previously published patient, so in-scope individuals are described.
method_note: Mutational-spectrum paper. Table 2 lists 54 unrelated families ('patients from 54 families that are not known to be related in whom SSADH deficiency was diagnosed'), so I gave one row to each of the 54 family-based patients; the paper's own label form is 'Patient 25' / 'Patient 21' / 'Patients 7 and 42', so I labelled them 'Patient <family no.>' and recorded family_label_in_paper as 'Family <n>' (the Table 2 cell prints only the number). Label spans quote the family-number cell of the patient's Table 2 row. Table 2's columns are NOT aligned to one another in this conversion: single cells hold stacks of values from several families (the line printed for families 4-6 carries six ethnic origins, and the remarks cell of the line printed for family 1 is 'Aoshima et al. [2002] c' although the patient of Aoshima et al. is the compound heterozygote with '103121del and 1460T > A', whose values sit on the line printed for families 2-3), so per D-31 I did not assign stacked cells to people by position and recorded variant description, ethnicity and source_reference_in_review as not reported for every patient; the only single-valued rows were family 1, family 33 and family 49, and even there the cross-column alignment could not be verified, so no variant or ethnic origin is reported from Table 2. Variants are recorded only where the text names the patient: Patient 21 (C223Y), Patient 25 (N255S), Patients 7 and 42 (G533R) and Patient 29 (heterozygous deletion of exons 2-5); the cDNA and protein strings and the class words for these come from the Table 3 rows that name exactly those variants. Every other patient keeps a variants row with variant_original_string 'not reported' because the paper ties ALDH5A1 variants to each family but the table conversion does not allow a reliable per-person attribution. The 56 probands' relatives from 22 families are described only as a count with no individual-level facts, so they get no rows. Variants the authors group as non-disease-causing (H180Y, P182L, G36R, A237S and the silent substitution) get no rows of their own; for Patient 29 the silent substitution is printed both as 'c.1389T4C' (codon D463) and as 'c.1398C4T' (D464D). No age, sex, consanguinity, treatment or vital status is given for any patient. Pathogenicity is 'not reported' everywhere because the authors' classifications are group statements ('Nine of the mutations ... can be considered causative for SSADH deficiency') that D-29 does not let me bind to one person's variant. One previously published patient is in scope because an individual-level feature is given ('patient who developed malignant neuroleptic syndrome after a single dose of haloperidol [Neu et al., 2002]'); that is why reports_individuals_with_tnfaip3_variant is true. Further uncertainties: the text writes 'G533K' where Table 3 prints 'G533R'; the text mentions 48, 54 and 55 families in different places and the relation between the 61 screened patients and the 54 families is not stated; Table 2's caption says 54 families while Table 3 counts 55. No script transcribed any table; every span was copied by hand from the paper, and only the repeated checklist and empty-field cells were generated by a short script from my reading.
